label: explain-track-3
one_line: We test whether a simple cell-shape model, locked in before looking, can predict dented hollow spaces in kidney-cell balls.
what: Many organs have a hollow space inside, called a lumen. Dog kidney cells grown in a gel form tiny balls with one such hollow. You might expect the hollow to be round, like a water balloon. In fact it is often dented. A 2021 study offered a simple idea: each cell brings a fixed length of inner wall, so cell count shapes the dents. We run no new lab work. We take that study's public measurements and public computer model. We tune the model on normal cells, lock the settings, then check it on cells it has not seen. It must beat plain guesses, such as "always round" or "use the average".
why: Faulty hollow spaces are tied to kidney and other disease. A popular idea says fluid pressure puffs the hollow into a smooth balloon. The 2021 study suggests pressure may matter less than cell number and inner wall per cell. Other labs disagree, so the question is still open. A test written down first is a fair way to make progress. We claim no cure and no medical effect.

steps.text: Download the public measurements from the 2021 paper and record a fingerprint of each file.
steps.picture: Like keeping a receipt and noting its total.

steps.text: Recompute the numbers that earlier helpers quoted. The ones we checked matched, but we did not redo them all.
steps.picture: Like adding up a shopping bill a second time.

steps.text: Fit a simple line on normal cells only. It links the number of cells to how dented the hollow is.
steps.picture: Like drawing a trend line through test scores from one school.

steps.text: Lock the settings in a dated file before looking at the other cell types.
steps.picture: Like sealing your exam answers in an envelope.

steps.text: Compare the model with plain guesses: always round, the average, and a line based on size alone.
steps.picture: Like asking whether a weather expert beats saying tomorrow will match today.

steps.text: Score the sealed answers on cells the model has not seen. The test is only partly blind, because the authors tuned two knobs and group averages were seen.
steps.picture: Like opening the envelope with a few hints already leaked.

steps.text: Split the data by photo day, because each cell type was imaged on different days. A cell-type gap cannot be told apart from a day gap.
steps.picture: Like comparing marks from two schools in two different years.

steps.text: Report the result in plain words, whether the model wins or loses.
steps.picture: Like posting the score even when your team lost.

wrong_if: Our written bet: the locked model will be no better than the size-only line on normal cells held out by photo day. If so, we were wrong. The model also fails if it cannot beat "always round" or "the average" on cells it has not seen.
could_go_wrong: The cell types were photographed on different days, so a real difference could be hidden by day-to-day noise.
Day-to-day spread in dentedness (about 0.07 on a 0-to-1 scale) is larger than some of the gaps we planned to detect.
The published model was tuned on the same data, so the test is only partly blind.
The authors' own code did not run as published, and our patched run did not clearly match their results.
The best setting of the published model sweep looked worse than a plain average on normal cells, so the first check may fail.
Two of the six planned tests lack enough data and may be dropped.
One formula in the plan was written upside down and must be fixed first.
Our law library has no law about lumen shape, so no proof tool backs the biology.

questions.q: How do you know the lumens are dented?
questions.a: The 2021 paper measured it. Roundness was about 0.3 to 0.7 on a scale where 1 is a perfect ball, and 10 to over 50 percent of the inner surface curved inward.

questions.q: How do you know the numbers are right?
questions.a: We re-ran scripts on the public files and got the quoted values. Each check was done by hand or script from the same files, but not every number was redone.
We did not rerun the Lean proofs, and we did not measure pressure ourselves. We also did not confirm the authors' simulation settings.
No. The model still includes pressure. Another lab measured about 65 pascals in these balls and says pressure matters more. We do not know who is right.

questions.q: Why not just run a new experiment?
questions.a: That would cost far more. Public data lets us run a fair first test cheaply.
If the locked model does no better than simple guesses on unseen cells. That would be reported.
One has too few cells, and another has only example images online. We would need to ask the authors for more.

questions.q: Does this say anything about medicine?
questions.a: No. It tests an idea about shape in lab-grown cells only.

glossary.plain: The hollow space inside a tube or ball of cells.
A standard type of lab-grown cell that forms small hollow balls.
The push of fluid against the wall of a space.
A unit of pressure; 65 pascals is a very small push, far less than a tyre holds.
A set of simple rules run on a computer to mimic something real.
Numbers fixed and dated before we look at new data.
Having parts of the wall that curve inward.
A score where 1 means perfectly smooth and round.
The face of each cell that points into the hollow.
A straight line drawn through points to show their overall pattern.
Cells whose results we keep hidden until the settings are locked.
Our list of rules that a computer has checked.
A computer run that imitates a real process.
The day a set of cells was imaged.
The raw tables a paper shares so others can check it.

check_yourself.expect: A paper on lumen shape in dog kidney cell balls, open access.

check_yourself.what: Open the independent lab data record.
check_yourself.expect: Three files; the example images file is 7467521 bytes.

check_yourself.what: Fingerprint the downloaded source data zip.

check_yourself.command: python an_power.py (in the t3-lumen-crit scripts folder)

check_yourself.what: Leave one photo day out and compare line against constant.
check_yourself.command: python an_loso.py (in the t3-lumen-crit scripts folder)

Notochord data 'cannot be a bounded-cost companion': a judgment, so not stated as fact.
Claim that all data-side numbers match 'exactly': the verifier called it too strong, so I said 'the ones we checked'.
Prediction that the published-sweep reproduction gate will fail: a forecast, not a sourced fact.
Need for an old NumPy and the authors' initial conditions: the agent's inference, not confirmed.
'Circular test' conclusion about identities: a judgment, so left out.
Advice to drop two tests and make two exploratory: a judgment; I said only that they may be dropped.
